channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: GitHub Discusses Accountability for AI Patch Flaws
item.description: GitHub’s Agentic Autofix can fix one vulnerability while creating another, raising accountability questions for patches. The tool re‑runs detection engines and project tests after patching, but can miss side effects, requiring validation and metric monitoring. Security teams should adjust CISO policies before deploying the agent, select models, and apply continuous testing to mitigate flaws.

item.title: Attacker Used 4,837 Hijacked GitHub Accounts to Run a CI Secret Stealer in 1,806+ Repositories
item.description: Starting Tuesday, an attacker used stolen credentials for 4,837 GitHub accounts to plant a secret stealer in repositories those accounts could write to, according to Aikido Security, a security software company. The stealer is built to take the secrets and cloud credentials that a repository's CI workflows can reach.

item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the freerdp component on its Enterprise Linux 10.0 Extended Update Support platform. Users should apply the update immediately to mitigate potential exploitation risks.

item.title: Red Hat httpd:2.4 Update Covers Important Vulnerability

item.title: Red Hat Issues Important Update for aspell

Administrators should apply the patch promptly to prevent exploitation and align with Red Hat’s security maintenance schedule.

item.title: Critical Apache HTTP/2 Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code Remotely
item.description: A critical flaw in Apache HTTP Server's HTTP/2 module, mod_http2, can let a remote attacker run code on the server. Tracked as CVE-2026-119618, it affects versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 and is fixed in version 2.4.71, released yesterday. Only servers with HTTP/2 enabled are affected, according to Red Hat, which ships the server as part of Red Hat Enterprise Linux.

item.title: ScreenConnect Targeted 288 Endpoints via Rogue Clients
item.description: ConnectWise reported unauthorized access incidents affecting at least 288 endpoints across 48 organizations using ScreenConnect with rogue client extensions. The company disabled five third‑party extensions in partner environments, noting no evidence of infrastructure compromise or software vulnerability in ScreenConnect itself. Security teams should monitor for rogue client activity, enforce extension whitelisting, and review access controls to mitigate similar threats.

item.title: ConnectWise ScreenConnect Compromised, SCKit Deployed
item.description: Attackers hijacked cloud‑hosted ConnectWise ScreenConnect panels and pushed the SCKit malware toolkit to at least 288 devices across 48 organizations. The compromise used unauthorized panel access to deploy code on each host, infecting all 288 devices within about 90 minutes. Huntress recommends auditing ScreenConnect credentials, enforcing MFA, and applying vendor security updates to block further exploitation.

item.title: Node.js Fixes 16 Security Flaws That Could Expose TLS Private Keys and Crash Servers Remotely
item.description: The Node.js project has released fixes for 16 security flaws across its 22.x, 24.x and 26.x lines. The official advisory says the patched builds are v22.23.5, v24.22.3 and v26.13.1. The update also refreshes three bundled parts: llhttp, undici, and sqlite.

item.title: MongoDB Use‑After‑Free CVE‑2026‑118383 Exploited
item.description: MongoDB is affected by CVE‑2026‑118383, a use‑after‑free vulnerability that can lead to arbitrary code execution in enterprise environments. The flaw arises when the database fails to release memory after a malicious request, allowing attackers to trigger a crash or execute injected code. MongoDB has released a patch; administrators should apply the update immediately and monitor logs for anomalous activity.

item.title: Apache RCE Flaw CVE-2026-119618 Requires Immediate Patch
item.description: A remote code execution flaw identified as CVE-2026-119618 targets Apache servers, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code in enterprise environments. The vulnerability stems from improper input validation in the request handling module, and public proof‑of‑concept exploits demonstrate its feasibility. Patch is available immediately; apply the latest Apache release or vendor‑issued hotfix and enable recommended detection rules.

item.title: Falcon C2 Targets Government Portals with JavaScript
item.description: Falcon C2 malware is targeting government portals by injecting malicious JavaScript into web pages. The injected scripts exploit client‑side vulnerabilities, capture user input, and establish command‑and‑control channels to exfiltrate data. Security teams should block known malicious domains, enforce script‑blocking policies, and immediately apply vendor security patches to mitigate the threat.

item.title: Git Six Flaw RCE Patches Released
item.description: Git released patches for six critical flaws that could enable remote code execution if an attacker crafts malicious repository data. The vulnerabilities involve deserialization of untrusted input and were identified through root‑cause telemetry and detection rule hunting. Security teams should apply the Git patches immediately and review detection rules to ensure coverage of the affected code paths.

item.title: Ivanti RCE Flaw CVE-2026-121683 Demands Prompt Patch
item.description: Ivanti software contains a remote code execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-121683, that permits attackers to run arbitrary code on affected systems. The flaw originates from unchecked user input in the configuration parser, and publicly available proof‑of‑concept code confirms exploitation. Security teams should immediately apply the Ivanti patch or upgrade to the latest release and enable the vendor‑issued detection rules.

item.title: ScreenConnect RCE Flaw Threatens Managed Service Providers
item.description: ScreenConnect, a support platform used by managed service providers, contains a remote code execution flaw that could allow attackers to execute arbitrary commands. The vulnerability arises from insufficient input validation in the session initiation module, and proof‑of‑concept exploits demonstrate its feasibility. Apply the vendor‑issued patch immediately, update to the latest ScreenConnect version, and enable the detection rules to mitigate risk.

item.title: Red Hat Patches gnome-remote-desktop Flaw in RHEL
item.description: Red Hat issued a security update addressing a vulnerability in the gnome-remote-desktop component for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8 Extended Update Support. The underlying flaw allows potential exploitation depending on system configuration, carrying a Red Hat severity rating of Important. Administrators using affected RHEL 9.8 Extended Update Support systems should apply the security patch immediately to mitigate risks.

item.title: Red Hat Releases python‑oauthlib Security Update
item.description: Red Hat has issued an Important security update for python‑oauthlib on RHEL 9.8 Extended Update Support, addressing multiple vulnerabilities identified by CVE references. The update includes CVSS scores for each vulnerability, but no active exploitation has been reported, mitigating potential remote code execution risks. Users should apply the RHSA‑2026:99167 update immediately to ensure protection against the disclosed weaknesses.

item.title: Chinese AI Project Gathers Taiwan Chip Industry Data
item.description: Chinese state-sponsored AI system collects data on Taiwan chip industry personnel. The system scrapes publicly available information and internal documents, building a database that could enable targeted exploitation of individuals abroad. Security teams should monitor for credential compromise, enforce strict access controls, and protect sensitive personnel data in the organization.

item.title: Red Hat Releases .NET 9.0 Update with Security Fixes
item.description: Red Hat released a .NET 9.0 update for RHEL 10 to fix multiple security issues. The update addresses several vulnerabilities with CVSS scores marked Important, though no specific CVE IDs are cited; the flaws could enable exploitation of the .NET runtime. Red Hat advises installing the package from standard RHEL repositories immediately and verifying checksums to ensure integrity.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Kernel Update for RHEL 10

Administrators should apply the RHSA‑2026:99133 package immediately to mitigate the identified flaws and ensure system reboot.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Kernel Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a kernel update for Enterprise Linux 10, fixing multiple security issues that could enable privilege escalation or denial of service. Apply the patch promptly to close the flaws, as it includes bug fixes and enhancements that address the reported weaknesses.

item.title: Red Hat Issues .NET 10.0 Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a .NET 10.0 security update for RHEL 10, addressing multiple vulnerabilities that could allow remote code execution via the .NET runtime. Red Hat recommends applying the RHSA-2026:99143 update immediately to mitigate potential exploitation.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Perl-DBI 1.641 Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the perl-DBI 1.641 module on RHEL 8. The update addresses multiple vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to gain elevated privileges or execute arbitrary code, as indicated by the CVSS scores linked in the advisory. Administrators should apply the patch immediately and verify module integrity to prevent exploitation.

item.title: ChromeOS LTS‑150 Patches Critical Use‑After‑Free
item.description: Google released ChromeOS LTS-150, patching numerous high‑severity CVEs including a critical CVE‑2026‑126879 use‑after‑free in the layout engine. The update addresses 18 CVEs such as CVE‑2026‑126901, CVE‑2026‑126856, and CVE‑2026‑126887, all of which could lead to code execution or denial of service.

item.title: Baker Tilly Clients Informed of Third‑Party Breach
item.description: Baker Tilly Advisory Group notified clients that a provider breach exposed personal information of clients and their dependents. The incident involved unauthorized access to sensitive data, including names, addresses, and financial details, though the full scope remains under investigation. Clients should monitor accounts, change passwords, and review security practices while Baker Tilly coordinates with the provider to assess impact.

item.title: Unit 42 Reveals AI‑Powered Red Team Tool Usage
item.description: Unit 42 identified adversaries deploying AI‑powered red team tools, such as ARTEX, to automate reconnaissance, credential harvesting, and lateral movement. These tools use large language models to generate phishing content, craft credential‑dump scripts, and orchestrate multi‑stage attack chains. Defenders should enable AI‑aware detection, enforce least‑privilege access, deploy MFA, and run regular red‑team simulations to validate controls.

item.title: ScreenConnect Malware Breaches MSPs, Targets Customer Devices
item.description: ConnectWise investigated a malware campaign that leveraged compromised ScreenConnect environments to deploy rogue remote‑access clients to customer devices of managed service providers. The attacks enabled attackers to gain remote control over client systems, potentially exfiltrating data and installing additional malicious payloads. ConnectWise recommends MSPs update ScreenConnect to the latest version, enforce strict access controls, and monitor for unauthorized remote‑access activity.

item.title: Arctic Wolf Highlights Agentic AI in 2026 Security Operations
item.description: Arctic Wolf’s 2026 Agentic Security Operations Report details how agentic AI collaborates with expert analysts to streamline incident response workflows. The integration reduces investigation time by up to 40 % and boosts detection accuracy, enabling quicker threat containment. Teams should evaluate agentic AI platforms, integrate them with SOAR, and train analysts to interpret AI‑generated hypotheses.

item.title: Greeter Attack Chain Leaves 'Hello' Trail in Cloud Logs
item.description: Researchers identified a new cloud attack chain named Greeter, in which adversaries embed 'hello' messages in log files to obscure their activity. The technique masks lateral movement and persistence indicators, making forensic analysis more difficult and delaying incident response. Defenders should enable log integrity monitoring, correlate anomalous 'hello' entries with known threat patterns, and apply stricter log retention policies.

item.title: eMudhra Revokes Eight CA Certificates After Key Mishap
item.description: eMudhra revoked eight intermediate CA certificates after discovering improper private key handling during certificate generation. The mishandling exposed the possibility of unauthorized certificate issuance, but no active exploitation has been reported. eMudhra has issued revocation notices, is reviewing its key management procedures, and will implement additional safeguards to prevent future incidents.

item.title: AI Enhances Cyber Resilience Competition
item.description: The article argues that AI technologies amplify both threat capabilities and defensive options, making rapid recovery a competitive advantage. It highlights how machine learning can detect anomalies faster, yet also enables adversaries to craft more sophisticated phishing and malware campaigns. Security teams should adopt AI‑driven monitoring, continuous testing, and adaptive response frameworks to mitigate evolving risks.

item.title: CVE-2026-125926 - Server-side request forgery in the server registration and update API in mcp-gateway-registry
item.description: Bulletin ID: 2026-180-AWS Publication Date: 11/11/2026 13:00 PM PST Description: MServer-side request forgery (SSRF) in the server registration and update API in Amazon mcp-gateway-registry before 1.35.0 might allow an authenticated remote user to send requests from the gateway to internal network services and cloud instance metadata endpoints and read the responses via a crafted request Impacted versions: >= v1.0.3 AND Refer to the article for the most up-to-date and complete information.

item.title: AWS mcp-gateway-registry Privilege Escalation via API
item.description: Amazon mcp-gateway-registry’s external management API lacks authorization, letting an authenticated user elevate to registry administrator. The flaw, present in versions 1.0.9–1.24.7, allows a crafted group import request to grant administrator scope to the attacker’s identity group, giving control over all registered gateway assets. AWS released a patch; security teams should upgrade to 1.24.8 or later and verify group import permissions.

item.title: Notion Breach Exposes AI Chat Transcripts
item.description: Notion revealed a breach at Fireworks AI that exposed AI chat transcripts from a few workspaces. Unauthorized access to Fireworks AI’s storage leaked user‑generated chat content, though no credentials were compromised. Notion advises users to review logs and reset passwords, while Fireworks AI has released a patch to secure the data.

item.title: N-able N-central Platform Offline Over 33 Flaws
item.description: N-able’s N-central RMM platform was taken offline after the discovery of 33 critical flaws that enable attacker takeover via public exploits. The vulnerabilities lack a single CVE identifier but collectively allow remote code execution and privilege escalation on affected installations. N-able released a hotfix; administrators should apply the update immediately and monitor for unauthorized access attempts.

item.title: Chrome Extended Stable Update 156.0.8078.100 Released
item.description: Google Chrome released Stable channel build 156.0.8078.100 for Windows and Mac, rolling out over the next weeks. The update includes security patches, but the full list of changes is available in the release log, and users are encouraged to review it. Users should install the update via browser settings or wait for automatic rollout to ensure protection against known vulnerabilities.
